Make her an idol trainee. Entertainment agencies teach all of those subjects nowadays.
Should I really try that?
So did the casting go well?
First we have to settle on the concept and build the right lineup around it.
What on earth are you guys planning to do?
Well, there was also some talk about a matchmaking concept.
That sounds great, matchmaking!
See that! Why did you not mention that idea first?
Do not worry about casting idols.
Because as chief producer, I will step right up to the front.

meanings.note: Casual exclamation used to call someone younger or a close friend.

examples.trans: Hey, come quickly!
Hey, where are you going?
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Contraction of 아이.
Colloquially used to refer to people of the same age or younger.

examples.trans: Kids are running around and playing in the park.
That person has a really good personality.
I want to give birth, have right now.
How about trying to give birth, have together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Auxiliary verb used after -지 to tell someone not to do something. Ending with -고 (말고) gives a brisk, trailing command. RR: malda.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.
Do not be late, and come early.
Did you hear about this education costs?
I was busy today because of education costs.

meanings.note: 답이 없다 ('there is no answer') is a common idiom meaning a situation is hopeless.

examples.trans: There's really no answer to this problem.
I found the answer to the question.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.en: to appear, be published, be achieved (a score/result)
meanings.note: Used for ratings, test scores, or results coming out

examples.trans: I came outside from the house.
The exam results came out well.
Did you hear about this idol?
I was busy today because of idol.
Did you hear about this trainee?
I was busy today because of trainee.

meanings.en: to make someone do, to assign work
meanings.note: Causative verb; e.g., 일을 시키다 'to assign work'.
E.g., 치킨을 시키다 'to order fried chicken'.

examples.trans: The team leader assigned this work to me.
Shall we order pizza for dinner?

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 요사이

examples.trans: How have you been doing these days?
I have too much work lately.
Did you hear about this at agencies?
I was busy today because of at agencies.

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.
I want to teach right now.
How about trying to teach together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Used for giving things to someone of equal or lower status.

examples.trans: I gave a gift.
Please give me some water.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?

meanings.note: adverb therefore

examples.trans: So how is it?
So I went.
Did you hear about this is casting?
I was busy today because of is casting.
Listen closely to what I explain.
I eat Korean food well.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.en: first, before others, ahead of time
meanings.note: Indicates priority in order or time.

examples.trans: It's late, so I'll head in first.
Who arrived first?

meanings.en: episode topic, segment idea, or concept (in TV production)
meanings.note: Loanword from English 'item'; writers and PDs use it for show ideas.

examples.trans: This week's episode topic is really good.
We are looking for a new segment idea.
Let's decide and together today.
I worked hard to decide and yesterday too.

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?

맞다.gloss: to be right, to be correct

meanings.note: Used to confirm facts or answers.

meanings.en: to fit, to suit, to match
meanings.note: E.g., 사이즈가 맞다 ('the size fits').

examples.trans: Yes, that's my phone number.
These shoes fit my feet perfectly.
Did you hear about this setup, lineup?
I was busy today because of setup, lineup.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.
Did you hear about this you guys?
I was busy today because of you guys.
How did you get here?
How should we solve this problem?

meanings.note: dummy

examples.trans: dummy trans 1
dummy trans 2

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?
Did you hear about this matchmaking, pairing?
I was busy today because of matchmaking, pairing.

meanings.note: dummy

examples.trans: dummy trans 1
dummy trans 2

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그것

examples.trans: Where did you buy that?
That is a really good idea.

좋다.gloss: to be good, to be nice

examples.trans: I feel really good today.
It's nice to take a walk in the morning.

meanings.en: see, told you so, look at that
meanings.note: contracted from 그거 보다 ('look at that'); commonly used as 거봐 or 거봐요

examples.trans: See, I was right, wasn't I?
Told you so, it's raining.
I want to humbly tell him right now.
How about trying to humbly tell him together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Often used with 하다.

examples.trans: Please don't worry.
I have many worries.
Did you hear about this chief, responsible?
I was busy today because of chief, responsible.

meanings.note: loanword from English 'producer', often abbreviated as PD (피디) in Korea

examples.trans: Seung-chan is a rookie producer at a broadcasting station.
Who is the producer of that variety show?

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
Did you hear about this to the forefront?
I was busy today because of to the forefront.
I want to will step forward right now.
How about trying to will step forward together tomorrow?
Did you hear about this since I intend to?
I was busy today because of since I intend to.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!
It is raining again.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.
